We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 5 reactions for target molecule: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We have guidance: steps enumerated forward: TBS protection, HWE, DIBAL-H reduction, TMSOTf protection, Still-Gennari reaction. But we need retrosynthetic steps (reverse). So we need to break down target into precursors via 5 steps, each corresponding to reverse of those forward reactions.

Thus we need to identify functional groups: there is a TBS protected alcohol? Actually target SMILES includes O[C@H]1... no TBS. Wait target includes O[C@H]1... maybe the TBS group already removed? The guidance mentions TBS protection as a step, but target may have free OH? The SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O. Contains an O attached to chiral carbon (primary alcohol). Also an O[C@@H]... an ether linking to side chain with conjugated diene and terminal aldehyde? Actually /C=C(CO)/C is a double bond with CHO? Wait C=C(CO)/C indicates a double bond with a CHO substituent? Actually (CO) is carbonyl? It's CO (aldehyde) attached to double bond carbon. So there is an aldehyde (CH=O) attached to double bond. Also a carboxylic acid at end: C(O)=O.

Thus forward steps: maybe start from simpler building blocks: 1) Protect alcohol with TBS (makes TBS ether). 2) Perform HWE to form C=C (E-alkene) linking side chain. 3) Reduce ester to aldehyde with DIBAL-H. 4) Protect another alcohol with TMSOTf? Not sure. 5) Still-Gennari to form Z-alkene? Hmm.

But we need retrosynthesis: target -> deprotect TBS (if present) -> precursor with free OH -> maybe precursor is product of HWE (i.e., a phosphonate + aldehyde). Then DIBAL-H reduction of ester to aldehyde. Then TMS protection of alcohol? Actually TMSOTf used to protect alcohol earlier, maybe later deprotected. Still-Gennari reaction forms Z-alkene from aldehyde and phosphonate.

Thus we can propose route:

Step 5 (last forward) Still-Gennari: forms Z-alkene from aldehyde and phosphonate ester. So retrosynthetic step: break the C=C double bond adjacent to carbonyl (the side chain) into aldehyde precursor and phosphonate. So we need to identify the double bond that was formed by Still-Gennari. In target, there is a conjugated diene: /C=C/C=C/. The first double bond (closest to ring) maybe from Still-Gennari? Actually there are two double bonds: one between C (attached to ring) and C (next). The second double bond between that C and next. The Still-Gennari likely forms the double bond adjacent to carbonyl (the terminal alkene with carboxylic acid). But not sure.

Simplify: propose 5 steps:

1) Deprotect TBS (if present) -> free alcohol. Use TBS deprotection (TBAF). But target has free OH, so preceding step would be TBS protected intermediate.

2) Remove TMS protecting group (if present) -> free alcohol.

3) Oxidize aldehyde to acid? Actually DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, so reverse is oxidation of aldehyde to ester (or use ester as precursor). So retrosynthetic step: aldehyde -> ester.

4) HWE: forms alkene from aldehyde + phosphonate. Reverse: alkene -> aldehyde + phosphonate.

5) Still-Gennari: forms Z-alkene from aldehyde + phosphonate (different). Might be similar to HWE but Z-selective.

We need to produce a JSON route with 5 reaction nodes, each with template_id (we need IDs). We have one template ID from earlier search: 29646 corresponds to deprotection of TBS? Actually template 29646 is retro: [C:2]-[OH]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-[Si]... i.e., protecting alcohol with TBS. So forward is protection; retro is deprotection. So we can use template_id 29646 for step 5 (deprotect TBS). Good.

Now need template for HWE (formation of alkene from aldehyde + phosphonate). Search for functional groups broken: "C-C double bonds" formed, "aldehydes" broken? Actually forward HWE: aldehyde + phosphonate -> alkene + carboxylate. So retro: alkene -> aldehyde + phosphonate. So we need a template where functional_groups_broken includes "C-C double bonds" and "carboxylic esters"? Not sure. Let's search for template with functional_groups_broken ["C-C double bonds"] and functional_groups_formed ["aldehydes", "carboxylic esters"] maybe.
